name: [WEEKLY] Public-facing app auth/authz bypass into server-side code execution (patch-bypass wave)
description: Detects the two-stage chain where an attacker abuses a public-facing web/app framework to defeat an authentication or authorization gate and then reaches server-side code execution — an anomalous shell, interpreter, or recon binary spawned by the web/app-server process (java, node, php, w3wp, httpd, nginx) within minutes of a suspicious write-verb or gadget-bearing HTTP request. This fortnight is dominated by 'incomplete-fix / patch-bypass' auth-bypass and RCE advisories: ApostropheCMS SSPP authorization bypass (CVE-2026-53609), Check Point SmartConsole auth bypass (CVE-2026-16232), VMware vCenter auth bypass + traversal RCE (CVE-2026-59309/59310), goshs empty-password SFTP bypass (CVE-2026-62325) and WebDAV MOVE bypass (CVE-2026-64863), OpenAM WebAuthn Java deserialization RCE (CVE-2026-62263), Velocity.js Function-constructor RCE, Pheditor forced-password-change bypass, kin-openapi fail-open NoopAuthenticationFunc, and Auth.js homoglyph normalization bypass. It spans the exploit → install/execution kill-chain: the HTTP stage carries the auth/authz-bypass or deserialization/SSTI marker, the endpoint stage is the framework process spawning an unexpected child or dropping a webshell. It FIRES when a server-tier process (not a browser/user shell) launches cmd/powershell/bash/curl/whoami-class children, or drops a new script under webroot, correlated to a preceding anomalous request; it does NOT fire on ordinary authenticated CRUD, on developer shells launched by IDEs, or on framework processes running their own bundled tooling under a service account with no post-request child spawn.
